findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body: Calling the disposer returned by `attach` no longer unregisters the `message` handler. Messages continue reaching disposed consumers, while repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate handlers and retained state. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` in the cleanup function.

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body: The interval handle is discarded and the returned cleanup does nothing. Consequently, `refresh` continues after disposal, repeated start/stop cycles accumulate timers, and the active interval can prevent Node.js from exiting. Retain and clear the timer in the cleanup function.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
After `attach()` returns, invoking its cleanup no longer unregisters the handler. Any later `"message"` still invokes disposed handlers, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and side effects.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the function returned by `startPolling()` no longer stops the interval. The refresh callback continues every second after cancellation, can mutate disposed state, and the referenced timer can prevent Node.js processes from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
After `attach()` returns, invoking its cleanup function no longer unregisters `handler`. If the socket remains active, subsequent messages still reach disposed consumers, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate listeners.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
`startPolling()` discards the timer handle and returns a no-op cleanup. After callers stop polling, `refresh` continues running every second; in Node.js the live interval can also prevent process or test shutdown indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer revokes the handler. A remote peer can continue delivering attacker-controlled messages to stale handlers after session teardown, potentially executing actions under an expired authorization context; repeated attach/dispose cycles also retain every handler and amplify each message.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the interval when polling is disposed
findings.body:
Every polling instance now remains active permanently and retains its callback. In an environment where an attacker can trigger repeated session/component creation, nominally disposed instances accumulate without bound, causing sustained callback work, memory retention, and eventual availability loss.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer removes the `"message"` handler. Long-lived sockets retain handlers and their captured state; repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate callbacks and memory usage.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the interval when polling is disposed
findings.body:
The interval handle is discarded and the returned disposer does nothing. After disposal, `refresh` continues every second and remains retained; repeated start/stop cycles accumulate timers, and in Node.js the referenced interval can prevent process shutdown indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
